evidence.excerpt: Long motor cables are common in industrial installations and amplify common-mode conducted disturbances by adding distributed capacitance to ground. This experimental study quantifies the effect for shielded and unshielded cables of lengths 5 m, 20 m, and 50 m connected to a 5.5 kW drive. CM conducted emission levels at the drive input were measured for each combination. Unshielded 50 m cables increased broadband CM noise by 10–14 dB relative to the 5 m reference below 1 MHz, primarily due to cable-to-ground capacitance estimated at 3.4 nF for the 50 m case. Shield grounding at both ends reduced CM emissions by 5–9 dB across 150 kHz–5 MHz for the 20 m cable. A transmission-line model incorporating per-unit-length parameters measured by time-domain reflectometry reproduced the resonant structure of the emission spectrum within ±3 dB. Practical wiring recommendations derived from the data are summarised for installation engineers.
